_meta.indication: CYRAMZA as a single agent is indicated for the treatment of patients with advanced or metastatic gastric or gastro-esophageal junction adenocarcinoma with disease progression on or after prior fluoropyrimidine- or platinum-containing chemotherapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of single-agent ramucirumab plus best supportive care versus placebo plus BSC
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic gastric cancer (including GEJ adenocarcinoma) with disease progression during or within 6 months after completion of platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-containing chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant OS improvement: median OS 5.2 vs 3.8 months; stratified HR 0.776 (95% CI 0.603, 0.998), log-rank p=0.0473. PFS also improved (HR 0.483, 95% CI 0.376, 0.620; p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), multicenter, multinational, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ramucirumab 8 mg/kg every two weeks in combination with paclitaxel compared with paclitaxel alone
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with previously treated metastatic or unresectable, locally advanced gastric cancer (recurrent or progressive metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma following platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary objective was overall survival; secondary objectives included progression-free survival, time-to-progression, and overall response rate
pivotal_trials.n: 665 patients randomized 1:1 (ramucirumab + paclitaxel vs paclitaxel alone)
pivotal_trials.result: Final analysis demonstrated a statistically significant effect on survival [HR 0.81 (0.68, 0.96), p = 0.02] and progression-free survival [HR 0.64 (0.54, 0.75), p<0.0001]; the effects on OS were consistently observed across relevant subgroups, including women and patients enrolled at sites in North America, Europe, or Australia.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and ≥2% higher than placebo) were hypertension (16% vs 8%) and diarrhea (14% vs 9%). Most common serious adverse events were anemia (3.8%) and intestinal obstruction (2.1%); red blood cell transfusions were given to 11% vs 8.7% of patients.
target_moa: Recombinant human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds the extracellular domain of VEGFR-2, blocking binding of its ligands (VEGF-A, VEGF-C, VEGF-D) and thereby inhibiting VEGF-stimulated angiogenesis
modality: mAb (recombinant human IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HEMORRHAGE — CYRAMZA increased the risk of hemorrhage, including severe and sometimes fatal hemorrhagic events; permanently discontinue in patients who experience severe bleeding.

rems.type: A REMS is not required to ensure safe use of ramucirumab in the indicated population.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee; application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected in the intended population.
